findings_and_fixes.original_issue: FormalApiListener assigned body_length=0 to a 204 without Content-Length and shut down after reading zero bytes; the HA empty-body assertion could hide illegal trailing application bytes.
findings_and_fixes.verified_fix: Worker sends TLS close_notify and flushes for the actual 204 Json reply. Client reads one additional byte and requires TLS EOF under the original deadline. The existing 307 drain/client-close/join path remains separate.

findings_and_fixes.original_issue: HTTPResponse.read applies the stdlib 204 zero-length shortcut and can hide bytes after headers; checking its decoded payload is insufficient.
findings_and_fixes.verified_fix: Before ordinary HTTPResponse.read, require absent Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding and an existing response.fp, then read one byte from that same original buffered stream and require EOF. No new connection or upload retry is introduced.

findings_and_fixes.original_issue: http_leaf used HTTPResponse.read and returned only decoded body bytes; Endpoint could neither see hidden 204 tail bytes nor validate original framing headers.
findings_and_fixes.verified_fix: The leaf owning the actual response checks CL/TE and reads original response.fp to EOF before returning an empty body. Endpoint retains its defensive empty-body check and original absolute subprocess budget.

findings_and_fixes.original_issue: Several restore phases retained only pre-upload generation and supplied a previous epoch from an older result or constant. A coincidental post-upload epoch could match that expectation without proving this upload advanced the actually observed source epoch.
findings_and_fixes.verified_fix: checked_before_capacity validates the existing actual pre-upload generation and epoch against the expected phase before any upload. publication then requires exact 204/empty body, post generation greater than actual before generation, and post epoch exactly actual before epoch plus one. All affected raw-upload call sites were reviewed. A phase-drift guard was authored but not run.

predicates: exact public sys/storage/raft/snapshot or sys/storage/raft/snapshot-force route
ordered_completion_before_204: terminal clock persistence and mandatory audit
applicable HA post-audit delivery proof and original owner checks
header_findings: The common HTTP writer uses no_body for 204, emits no Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding, and emits no body bytes.
Quota and consistency metadata, including X-Vault-Index, remain on the final response.
Transport-owned control headers cannot be injected through ordinary response metadata.
Quota metadata application failure returns 503 and cannot be mapped to 204.

exclusions.reason: Distinct PendingRestore observation; successful reconciliation retains 200 JSON.
Exact public route predicate is false; original response remains.
Not a public POST/PUT Upload; file and HEAD behavior remain.
Trusted redirect metadata is handled before 204 conversion.
No successful Upload classification or final status is not 200.
Existing non-200 failure and reconciliation metadata remain; conversion does not erase them.

production_mapping.internal_service_and_audit_status: The internal Service success and its audit semantics remain 200; this is a public HTTP response mapping, not a claim of full audit-field parity.

harness_integrity.capacity_observation_limit: Adjacent authenticated capacity observations in an owned fixture are not a transactional operation receipt. uploaded_archive_generation labels the uploaded archive; observed_local_generation labels the later observation. Actual archive effect still requires full values, marker rollback, Raft and cold-reopen checks.
harness_integrity.gated_timing_limit: Additional read-only capacity observations consume the existing provider gate time. No 2.7-second gate was relaxed; its feasibility still requires execution.

execution_limits.review_kind: static source review, local hash/diff calculation and read-only stdlib source inspection
execution_limits.new_stdlib_guard: Authored test uses the real HTTPResponse parser with a BytesIO-backed fake socket. It was not run, creates no real TLS evidence, and cannot qualify production behavior.
execution_limits.eof_error_limit: EOF read errors propagate for non-expire requests; the original expire case remains a non-success outcome. An EOF timeout runtime negative was not executed.
